banner.title: ROGUES BEYOND 20TH - DMO Chapter 7, round four of five: the rogue advancement grid (the printed body caption reads Table 47 - the same number the priest spell progression caption printed - with 2,200,000 XP at 20th in 220K steps and the printed 120K final step to 4,300,000 at 30th, weapon and nonweapon proficiencies, the 10+N d6 hit points with the Con-bonus-after-10th footnote), the thieving doctrine (the 95 percent cap below 11th, no limit from 11th, 96-or-higher automatic failure, penalties from the base score), the five new thieving skills with their base scores and the racial, Dexterity-aim and armor adjustment grids (Tables 48 through 51), the thief powers (five skills at 21st, 50 S&P character points with the 9-skill overflow rule, the 24th-level scroll ladder at 25 percent), the bard powers (two skills at 21st, 20 points, the 21st-level scroll ladder at 15 percent, 55 percent item identification, wands at 24th, item creation at 27th) with the Table 52 bard spell progression, and all eleven rogue skills (adaptation, classify traps, evasion, fall and jump, featherfoot, improvised attack, inner focus, nondetection, sense danger, shadow flight and shadow travel).
banner.provenance: verified against printed pp. 167-177 of the archive.org DMO captures (items dungeon-master-option-high-level-campaigns and tsr02156dmsoptionhighlevelcampaigns, the djvu.txt full texts; the tsr02156 ABBYY read is primary and the tesseract read is cross-checked; leaf N = printed page N). TWO contested cells settled against the physical copy (user-confirmed 2026-10-18): the Table 47 level-30 experience print reads 4,300,000 (the ABBYY read; tesseract read 4,500,000 and the series would give 4,400,000) with the final step only 120,000 points; and the Table 50 tunneling row prints a dash at Dexterity 17 and +30 percent at Dexterity 22 (the tesseract read; the ABBYY capture dropped the final cell). TWO more printed quirks held: the rogue advancement caption shares the printed number 47 with the priest spell progression caption (whose contents entry reads 46); and the Table 49 halfling detect magic cell prints +5 without the percent sign its row siblings carry.

bools.name: dfaThief95CapSpendElsewhere
bools.comment: the thieving cap doctrine: once a single skill reaches 95 percent the character must spend discretionary points on other skills (printed p. 167).

bools.name: dfaThiefAll95PointsLost
bools.comment: the thieving cap doctrine: if all the thieving skill scores are 95 percent, the discretionary points are lost (printed p. 167).

bools.name: dfaThiefLostPointsNotRegained
bools.comment: the thieving cap doctrine: discretionary points the character lost earlier are not regained when the cap is lifted at 11th level (printed p. 167).

bools.name: dfaThiefPenaltiesFromBase
bools.comment: the thieving penalty rule: any penalties to the roll are subtracted from the base score (printed p. 167).

bools.name: dfaT47FinalStepShort
bools.comment: the Table 47 printed quirk: the final 29th-to-30th experience step is only 120,000 points, not the 220,000-point series the first ten steps follow (settled against the physical copy, user-confirmed 2026-10-18) (printed p. 168).

bools.name: dfaT47ConBonusStopsAfter10
bools.comment: the Table 47 footnote: bonus hit points from high Constitution scores are not added after 10th level - the rogue footnote reads 10TH where the warrior and wizard tables read 9th (pinned verbatim) (printed p. 168).

bools.comment: the Table 47 caption duplication: this body caption prints Table 47, the same printed number the priest spell progression body caption uses on printed p. 161 (whose contents entry reads Table 46) - the printed book numbers two different tables 47 (printed pp. 161, 168).

bools.name: dfaBribeOneAttemptPerTarget
bools.comment: the bribe doctrine: only one bribe can be attempted per target (printed pp. 168-169).

bools.name: dfaBribeFailReactionRoll
bools.comment: the bribe doctrine: if the attempt fails the DM makes a reaction roll for the target to determine how he counters the bribe (printed pp. 168-169).

bools.name: dfaBribeNotEveryoneSusceptible
bools.comment: the bribe doctrine: the DM must decide if the NPC in question can be bribed - not everyone is susceptible (printed pp. 168-169).

bools.name: dfaBribeNotOutsideStation
bools.comment: the bribe doctrine: no character can be bribed to do something that falls outside his job or station (printed pp. 168-169).

bools.name: dfaBribeNeverDangerousOrLong
bools.comment: the bribe doctrine: a bribed NPC does not perform any action that takes more than a few minutes of effort or places himself in danger - the task must strike the character as quick and harmless (printed pp. 168-169).

bools.name: dfaBribeNeverAgainstBeliefs
bools.comment: the bribe doctrine: a simple bribe never induces a character to compromise something he believes in (printed pp. 168-169).

bools.name: dfaBribeSecretReactionRoll
bools.comment: the bribe procedure: secretly roll 1d20 against Table 59 of the Dungeon Master Guide and do not tell the player the reaction - simply role play the response (printed pp. 168-169).

bools.name: dfaBribeFriendlyNeedsNoBribe
bools.comment: the bribe procedure: if the reaction roll is friendly the NPC probably does what the thief wants without a bribe (printed pp. 168-169).

bools.name: dfaBribeMultiplyByDifference
bools.comment: the bribe procedure: the amount required is the status table roll multiplied by the difference between the reaction roll and the highest number on Table 59 that is a friendly result (printed pp. 168-169).

bools.name: dfaBribePlayerNeverToldValues
bools.comment: the bribe procedure: the player should never be told the NPC station, the base bribe value, or the initial reaction roll (printed p. 169).

bools.name: dfaDetectIllusionNeedsRound
bools.comment: the detect illusion doctrine: detection is not automatic - the thief must spend a round concentrating on the area of effect (printed p. 169).

bools.name: dfaDetectIllusionTranslucent
bools.comment: the detect illusion doctrine: the thief perceives the illusion as a translucent image, as though it were a light mist - the more real the illusion the more solid the image (printed p. 169).

bools.name: dfaDetectIllusionNotVsNonvisible
bools.comment: the detect illusion doctrine: invisibility and other nonvisible effects cannot be discerned (printed p. 169).

bools.name: dfaDetectIllusionNotFailSafe
bools.comment: the detect illusion doctrine: knowing that something is an illusion is not necessarily a fail-safe defense, such as in the case of a simulacrum (printed p. 169).

bools.name: dfaDetectMagicBlockedLikeSpell
bools.comment: the detect magic doctrine: the ability can be blocked by the same things that prevent detect magic spells from operating (printed p. 169).

bools.name: dfaEscapeBondsRollPerDevice
bools.comment: the escape bonds doctrine: the thief must roll to break free of every device binding him - tied at wrists and ankles means two successful rolls (printed p. 169).

bools.name: dfaEscapeBondsLockedNeedPicks

bools.name: dfaEscapeBondsFailCantRetryThatBond

bools.name: dfaTunnelCollapseOnFail

bools.name: dfaTunnelRedugAtLooseRate

bools.comment: the bard scroll doctrine: wizard scrolls of a level the bard can cast are read with no chance of failure (printed pp. 170-171).

bools.name: dfaBardIdentifyNoBonusesCharges
bools.comment: the bard item identification limit: the item exact magical bonuses and number of charges are never revealed (printed p. 171).

bools.name: dfaBardIdentifyNoHandling
bools.comment: the bard item identification doctrine: the bard need not handle the item or expend any materials - merely examining it closely (printed p. 171).

bools.name: dfaAdaptLikeWarriorSkill
bools.comment: the adaptation doctrine: except where noted the rogue skill is identical to the warrior skill of the same name (printed p. 171).

bools.name: dfaAdaptNoSituationalOrNoncombat
bools.comment: the adaptation limit: the skill does not allow characters to ignore situational movement penalties or environmental factors that are not combat related, or conditions that are physically impossible to overcome (printed p. 171).

bools.name: dfaAdaptNoMagicalOrVisionPenalties
bools.comment: the adaptation limit: the skill has no effect on penalties derived from an environment magical properties or on penalties based on vision or lighting (printed p. 171).

bools.name: dfaAdaptCheckEachRound
bools.comment: the adaptation procedure: at the end of each round in combat the character checks the skill - it requires only a moment thought, can be checked every round until successful, and does not prevent other actions (printed pp. 171-172).

bools.name: dfaAdaptLastsBattlePlusDays
bools.comment: the adaptation duration: once the skill succeeds the character temporarily ignores the environment special effects for the entire battle plus one day per character level thereafter (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaAdaptPermanentBeforeFade
bools.comment: the adaptation permanent gate: the permanent adjustment holds only if the additional cost is paid before the adaptation fades (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaClassifyNeedsFindTraps
bools.comment: the classify traps limit: the skill is useless without the find traps ability (printed pp. 171-172).

bools.name: dfaClassifyRevealsExactNature
bools.comment: the classify traps doctrine: a successful roll reveals the trap exact nature - how it works, what it does to people who trigger it, and where its attacks are aimed provided the rogue can observe those areas (printed pp. 171-172).

bools.name: dfaClassifyMagicalHalvedRoundUp
bools.comment: the classify traps limit: a magical or invisible trap reduces the rogue success number, including ability score bonuses, by half with fractions rounded up (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaClassifyFailUnder20LearnsNothing
bools.comment: the classify traps doctrine: a failed roll of less than 20 means the rogue cannot determine anything special about the trap (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaClassifySecretRoll
bools.comment: the classify traps doctrine: the DM should make the skill roll secretly (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaClassifyTwoRemoveRollsBest
bools.comment: the classify traps disarm option: after a successful examination the character can make two remove traps rolls taking only the best result (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaClassifyBypassSaveVsBreath
bools.comment: the classify traps bypass option: the rogue can trigger the trap from a safe place - if complete avoidance is impossible the rogue saves vs. breath weapon, is unharmed on success, and takes half damage on failure (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaClassifyCompanionsMaySave
bools.comment: the classify traps companion option: companions warned by the rogue can attempt breath weapon saving throws to avoid the effects and suffer only half damage on a failed save (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaClassifyNoHalfEffectRuling
bools.comment: the classify traps doctrine: when a trap attack cannot have a half effect the DM can require another saving throw against the trap attack form or rule that characters are fully effected when they fail the breath weapon saving throw (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaEvasionAutomatic
bools.comment: the evasion doctrine: the skill operates automatically whenever a rogue is subjected to an energy attack that causes damage (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaEvasionNoDamageOnSave
bools.comment: the evasion doctrine: the rogue rolls a normal saving throw vs. the effect and suffers no damage if it is successful (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaEvasionNotVsNonDamage
bools.comment: the evasion limit: the skill is not effective against effects that do not inflict damage or that do not normally allow a saving throw - a bronze dragon repulsion breath, a gorgon petrifying breath or magic missile spells (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaEvasionFixedMissilesOnly
bools.comment: the evasion missile rule: the rogue can avoid missiles fired from fixed points such as traps and siege engines, but not from creatures (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaEvasionNeedsNotSurprised
bools.comment: the evasion missile rule: if not surprised the rogue avoids the missile with a successful saving throw vs. breath weapon (printed p. 172).

bools.name: dfaFallAlwaysWithinOneFoot
bools.comment: the fall/jump surface rule: rogues who simply step off a precipice or fall while climbing are always within one foot of a vertical surface unless it has a negative slope (printed p. 173).

bools.name: dfaFallFrictionSurfacesOk
bools.comment: the fall/jump surface rule: any surface that can provide a reasonable amount of friction is sufficient (ropes, tree trunks, walls) while very smooth or slippery surfaces are useless (ice walls, greased poles, walls of force) (printed p. 173).

bools.name: dfaFallDamageOnExcess
bools.comment: the fall/jump damage rule: if the fall is longer than the safe distance allowed for the rogue level, subtract the safe distance from the total distance before determining damage from the fall (printed p. 173).

bools.name: dfaFeatherNeedsMoveSilently
bools.comment: the featherfoot gate: the skill is a function of the rogue move silently ability, which is a requirement for using this skill (printed p. 173).

bools.name: dfaFeatherMustStopAtDistance
bools.comment: the featherfoot limit: the rogue must stop and make contact with the surface after moving the allowed distance (printed p. 173).

bools.name: dfaFeatherSilentNoTracks
bools.comment: the featherfoot doctrine: the character moves in complete silence and leaves no tracks on the ground, and the character weight does not press down upon the surface at all (printed p. 173).

bools.name: dfaFeatherNoWeightTriggers
bools.comment: the featherfoot doctrine: the character does not set off any alarm or trap triggered by weight and does not trigger a squeaking floors spell (printed p. 173).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedLearnMultipleTimes
bools.comment: the improvised attack doctrine: each time the rogue learns the skill again the daily allotment grows by one (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedBlindfightingNoHelp
bools.comment: the improvised attack blinding note: the blindfighting proficiency does not reduce the penalties, and many creatures cannot be blinded because they have no visual organs (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedDisarmStuckNeedsOpenDoors
bools.comment: the improvised attack disarm effect: the opponent saves vs. petrification or loses the use of one weapon; recovering a dropped weapon takes a half move and a stuck weapon needs a successful open doors roll (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedKillHigherHdImmune
bools.comment: the improvised attack kill limit: opponents with more Hit Dice or a higher level than the rogue are immune to kill effects and take normal damage (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedStunNoSpellsAttack
bools.comment: the improvised attack stun doctrine: a stunned character is unable to cast spells, attack, or move at more than half speed (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedAnnounceDeclareDescribe
bools.comment: the improvised attack procedure: the attack must be announced in the declaration phase and described exactly in the resolution phase - a simple called shot never qualifies (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedNormalAttackRoll
bools.comment: the improvised attack procedure: the rogue makes a normal attack roll with standard combat modifiers; the backstab bonus applies to rear attacks, the Dexterity/Aim missile bonus usually applies, and Strength/Muscle bonuses apply to blows (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedSuccessNoDamage
bools.comment: the improvised attack doctrine: if the attack succeeds the opponent suffers no damage but must roll a saving throw or suffer the special effect (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedSaveUnlikelyRange
bools.comment: the improvised attack save modifier: plus 2 to plus 6 if the attack described is physically unlikely to have the desired effect (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedSaveAutoIfInadequate
bools.comment: the improvised attack save modifier: the save is automatic if the method described is completely inadequate (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedTable3638Optional
bools.comment: the improvised attack option: the optional saving throw modifiers from Table 36 or Table 38 can be applied if the DM wishes (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedTrickThreeAdventures
bools.comment: the improvised attack trick establishment: if a rogue has successfully used the same improvised attack in three separate adventures the character can purchase the skill again at the next level to make the trick a permanent part of the character skills (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedTrickOncePerEncounter
bools.comment: the improvised attack trick doctrine: an established trick can be used once per encounter without the usual penalty for multiple use, though situational penalties still apply (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedTrickNotDailyAllotment
bools.comment: the improvised attack trick doctrine: using an established trick does not count toward the daily allotment unless the trick is used more than once in a single encounter (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaImprovisedTrickPreparedPlus6
bools.comment: the improvised attack trick doctrine: opponents who have fought the rogue previously and are prepared for an established trick gain a plus 6 saving throw bonus against it (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaJobareHatBlindExample
bools.comment: the Jobare trick hat example: the DM and player agree the clamped hat is a blinding attack, the attack succeeds, and the man fails his save vs. breath weapon at minus 2 - later Jobare establishes the trick hat as a permanent skill (printed p. 174).

bools.name: dfaFocusLikeWarriorSkill
bools.comment: the inner focus doctrine: the rogue skill marshals personal energies to provide a temporary bonus to Dexterity, Intelligence or Constitution scores and is otherwise similar to the warrior skill of the same name (printed p. 175).

bools.name: dfaFocusAlreadyHigherNoEffect
bools.comment: the inner focus ceiling: if the character ability score is already higher than the value listed on the table this skill has no effect - the priest wording again, not the wizard equal to or higher (pinned verbatim) (printed p. 175).

bools.name: dfaFocusEndAtWill
bools.comment: the inner focus doctrine: the rogue can end the boost - and restore the values of the other two ability scores - at any time (printed p. 175).

bools.name: dfaFocusSubabilitiesRaisedEqual
bools.comment: the inner focus doctrine: under the optional subabilities rule both subabilities scores in the increased ability are raised to the same value (printed p. 175).

bools.name: dfaFocusOneBoostAtATime
bools.comment: the inner focus limit: a character can have only one ability score improvement from this skill operating at any given time (printed p. 175).

bools.name: dfaFocusNoOtherActions
bools.comment: the inner focus procedure: the rogue can take no other actions during the round spent concentrating on raising the selected ability score (printed p. 175).

bools.name: dfaFocusBonusesImmediate
bools.comment: the inner focus doctrine: bonuses from an increased score are applied immediately when the skill succeeds and are immediately lost when the boost duration ends - reduced score effects are likewise restored when the improvement ends (printed p. 175).

bools.name: dfaNondetectionBeatsDivinations
bools.comment: the nondetection doctrine: a successful skill check defeats a spell such as ESP, clairaudience or detect invisibility, or a magical item such as a crystal ball (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaNondetectionSavesEvenOnFail
bools.comment: the nondetection doctrine: even if the roll fails the rogue is still entitled to any applicable saving throws (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaNondetectionBeatsSenseDanger
bools.comment: the nondetection reach: the skill is also effective against the sense danger skill (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaNondetectionBeatsDetectDeception
bools.comment: the nondetection reach: the skill is also effective against the priest detect deception skill (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaNondetectionOpposedWillpower
bools.comment: the nondetection procedure: when subjected to one of these powers the rogue can attempt an opposed Wisdom/Willpower check to remain undetected (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaNondetectionNotVsFourSpells
bools.comment: the nondetection limit: the skill is not effective against know alignment, true seeing, commune or contact other plane (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaNondetectionNotVsLegendaryOrDeities
bools.comment: the nondetection limit: the skill is not effective against the detection abilities of legendary monsters, wyrm and great wyrm dragons, or deities (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseSecondPurchaseExtra
bools.comment: the sense danger doctrine: if the character purchases this skill twice the rogue gains one extra subskill (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseImprovesAllSubskills
bools.comment: the sense danger doctrine: any improvement to the skill number improves all the subskills the character knows (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseAmbushOncePerTurn
bools.comment: the sense danger ambush limit: an area can be scanned only once each turn (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseAmbushRevealsCountAndSize
bools.comment: the sense danger ambush doctrine: a successful scan reveals approximately how many creatures are hiding in the area and their approximate size (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseConcealedRevealsSizeLocationType
bools.comment: the sense danger concealed weapons doctrine: a successful check reveals the weapon general size, location and type (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseUnknownCreatureAttackModes
bools.comment: the sense danger concealed weapons doctrine: faced with an unknown creature a successful check determines its attack modes (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseMagicalConcealmentDetected
bools.comment: the sense danger concealed weapons note: unlike the warrior version a rogue can detect magically concealed weapons (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseHostilityNotPreparedness
bools.comment: the sense danger hostile intentions doctrine: a successful roll gives a general level of hostility - low, medium or high - but not how well prepared the creature is, nor how likely it is to attack (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseImpendingDirectionAndDistance
bools.comment: the sense danger impending attacks doctrine: the rogue receives a vague impression of the attacker general direction (front, rear, left, right) and distance (close, far) (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseImpendingMustFace
bools.comment: the sense danger impending attacks limit: unlike the warrior back protection the rogue must turn to face the attacker to negate rear attack bonuses - if surprised the attacker receives all rear attack bonuses including backstab adjustments (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseSecretRolls
bools.comment: the sense danger procedure: the DM should roll the check secretly (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaSenseFalseNotImpending
bools.comment: the sense danger false indication: it has no effect on an impending attack (printed p. 176).

bools.name: dfaFlightLikeShadowTravel
bools.comment: the shadow flight doctrine: the ability is similar to the shadow travel skill except a successful hide in shadows roll allows the character to fly silently from shadow to shadow (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaFlightNeedsHideInShadows
bools.comment: the shadow flight procedure: the rogue must begin with a successful hide in shadows roll (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaFlightNoFlightWithoutShadow
bools.comment: the shadow flight limit: with no shadow flight is not possible and movement is normal (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaFlightLeapNeedsAsShadowy
bools.comment: the shadow flight leap limit: the destination must be at least as shadowy as the rogue current position (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaFlightLightEncumbranceOnly
bools.comment: the shadow flight limit: while flying or traveling instantaneously the rogue can be no more than lightly encumbered (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaFlightCarryWithinLimit
bools.comment: the shadow flight limit: the rogue can carry other creatures if their weight does not exceed the light encumbrance limit (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaShadowNeedsHideInShadows
bools.comment: the shadow travel procedure: the rogue must first successfully hide in shadows, which is required to use this skill (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaShadowNoShadowsNormal
bools.comment: the shadow travel limit: with no shadows available the movement rate is normal (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaShadowVisibleBetweenShadows
bools.comment: the shadow travel doctrine: the rogue is visible when moving between shadows but remains hidden while within them (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaShadowEndsOnAttack
bools.comment: the shadow travel doctrine: accelerated movement lasts until the character attacks or the shadows get weaker; the rogue can re-enter and resume on any round without an attack (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaShadowNotSilent
bools.comment: the shadow travel doctrine: shadow movement is not silent, but the rogue can attempt a move silently roll while moving through shadows and still move at the accelerated rate (printed p. 177).

bools.name: dfaShadowTerrainAndEncumbranceApply
bools.comment: the shadow travel doctrine: accelerated movement is subject to normal modifiers for terrain and encumbrance (printed p. 177).

chains.name: dfaThiefScrollBand
chains.comment: the thief scroll ladder: thief levels 23 or less band 0 (no scroll use), 24-26 band 1 (1st-level scrolls), 27-28 band 2 (2nd-level scrolls), and 29 or more the tail band 3 (3rd-level scrolls) (printed p. 170).

chains.name: dfaBardScrollBand
chains.comment: the bard scroll ladder: bard levels 20 or less band 0 (no scroll use), 21-23 band 1 (1st), 24-26 band 2 (2nd), 27-29 band 3 (3rd), and 30 or more the tail band 4 (4th-level scrolls) (printed pp. 170-171).

chains.name: dfaFallBand
chains.comment: the fall/jump level ladder: rogue levels 11-13 band 0 (30 feet), 14-16 band 1 (60), 17-19 band 2 (90), 20-21 band 3 (120), 22-24 band 4 (150), 25-27 band 5 (180), and 28 or more the tail band 6 (210) - the safe fall distance is 30 feet plus 30 feet per band (printed pp. 172-173).

chains.name: dfaFeatherBand
chains.comment: the featherfoot level ladder: rogue levels 11-13 band 0 (soft surfaces), 14-16 band 1 (very soft surfaces), and 17 or more the tail band 2 (liquid surfaces) (printed p. 173).

chains.name: dfaFocusBand
chains.comment: the inner focus boost ladder: rogue levels 11-15 band 0 (boost to 18), 16-20 band 1 (19), 21-25 band 2 (20), and 26 or more the tail band 3 (21) - the improved score is 18 plus the band (printed p. 175).

chains.name: dfaSenseBand
chains.comment: the sense danger subskill ladder: rogue levels 15 or less band 0 (skill unavailable), 16-20 band 1 (one subskill), 21-25 band 2 (two subskills), and 26 or more the tail band 3 (three subskills) - the subskill count is the band (printed pp. 176-177).

tables.name: dfaT47Grid
tables.comment: the Table 47 rogue advancement grid (printed p. 168): eleven rows for levels 20 through 30 (row index = level minus 20) - experience points, weapon and nonweapon proficiency counts, and the 10-plus-N d6 hit-point cells read as the constant 10 base plus the per-level bonus. The tag T47r distinguishes this grid from the priest spell progression grid that shares the printed caption number 47.
col_comments: the experience column: 2,200,000 at 20th in 220,000 steps to 4,180,000 at 29th, then the printed 120,000 final step to 4,300,000 at 30th (printed p. 168).
the weapon proficiency column: 7, 7, 7, 7, 8, 8, 8, 8, 9, 9, 9 across levels 20-30 (printed p. 168).
the nonweapon proficiency column: 8, 8, 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 9, 10, 10, 10 - one more every four levels (printed p. 168).
the hit-point base column: the constant 10 of the printed 10-plus-N cells (printed p. 168).
the hit-point bonus column: 20 at 20th rising in plus-two steps to 40 at 30th (printed p. 168).

tables.name: dfaT49Grid
tables.comment: the Table 49 thieving skill racial adjustment grid (printed p. 169): five rows (bribe, detect illusion, detect magic, escape bonds, tunneling) by six race columns (dwarf, elf, gnome, half-elf, halfling, human). The printed dashes read as zero - no racial adjustment; the halfling detect magic cell prints +5 without the percent sign.
col_comments: the dwarf column: minus 5 on bribe, plus 5 on detect illusion, plus 5 on detect magic, no escape bonds adjustment, plus 10 on tunneling (printed p. 169).
the elf column: plus 15 on bribe, no detect illusion adjustment, plus 10 on detect magic, no escape bonds adjustment, minus 10 on tunneling (printed p. 169).
the gnome column: plus 5 on bribe, plus 10 on detect illusion, plus 5 on detect magic, no escape bonds adjustment, plus 5 on tunneling (printed p. 169).
the half-elf column: plus 5 on bribe, plus 5 on detect illusion, plus 5 on detect magic, no escape bonds adjustment, minus 5 on tunneling (printed p. 169).
the halfling column: no bribe, detect illusion or detect magic adjustment beyond the printed +5 cell, plus 10 on escape bonds, plus 5 on tunneling (printed p. 169).
the human column: no racial adjustments on any of the five skills (printed p. 169).

tables.name: dfaT50Grid
tables.comment: the Table 50 Dexterity/Aim adjustment grid (printed p. 170): two rows (escape bonds and tunneling) by ten Dexterity columns (9, 10, 11, 12-16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22). The printed dashes read as zero; the tunneling row prints a dash at Dexterity 17 and +30 percent at 22.
col_comments: the Dexterity 9 column: escape bonds minus 15, tunneling minus 10 (printed p. 170).
the Dexterity 10 column: escape bonds minus 10, tunneling minus 5 (printed p. 170).
the Dexterity 11 column: escape bonds minus 5, tunneling no adjustment (printed p. 170).
the Dexterity 12-16 column: no adjustment on either skill (printed p. 170).
the Dexterity 17 column: escape bonds plus 5, tunneling the printed dash (no adjustment) (printed p. 170).
the Dexterity 18 column: escape bonds plus 10, tunneling plus 5 (printed p. 170).
the Dexterity 19 column: escape bonds plus 15, tunneling plus 10 (printed p. 170).
the Dexterity 20 column: escape bonds plus 20, tunneling plus 15 (printed p. 170).
the Dexterity 21 column: escape bonds plus 25, tunneling plus 20 (printed p. 170).
the Dexterity 22 column: escape bonds plus 30, tunneling the printed plus 30 (printed p. 170).

tables.name: dfaT51Grid
tables.comment: the Table 51 thieving skill armor adjustment grid (printed p. 170): three rows (bribe, escape bonds, tunneling) by three armor columns (no armor, elven chain, padded or studded leather).
col_comments: the no armor column: bribe minus 10, escape bonds plus 5, tunneling plus 10 (printed p. 170).
the elven chain column: bribe plus 5, escape bonds minus 5, tunneling minus 5 (printed p. 170).
the padded or studded leather column: bribe minus 5, escape bonds minus 5, tunneling minus 10 (printed p. 170).

tables.name: dfaBribeGrid
tables.comment: the bribe status grid (printed pp. 168-169): four NPC stations (peasant or slave, freeman or soldier, merchant or officer, noble or general) each with a dice count and die size in copper pieces.
col_comments: the bribe dice column: 2d4 for a peasant or slave, 3d8 for a freeman or soldier, 5d10 for a merchant or officer, 5d100 for a noble or general (printed pp. 168-169).
the bribe die size column: the second number of each dice notation - 4, 8, 10 and 100 (printed pp. 168-169).

tables.name: dfaTunnelGrid
tables.comment: the tunneling earth grid (printed p. 169): three earth types (sand or loose earth, packed earth, rock) each with a skill modifier and a digging time in hours per 10 foot tunnel. The packed earth dash reads as zero modifier.
col_comments: the earth modifier column: minus 10 for sand or loose earth, zero for packed earth, plus 10 for rock (printed p. 169).
the earth hours column: 5 hours for sand or loose earth, 10 for packed earth, 30 for rock (printed p. 169).

tables.name: dfaT52Grid
tables.comment: the Table 52 bard spell progression grid (printed p. 171): eleven rows for levels 20 through 30 (row index = level minus 20) by eight spell level columns. The printed dashes read as zero - the bard cannot yet cast spells of that level.
col_comments: the 1st-level column: 4 through 24th, 5 from 25th, 6 from 28th (printed p. 171).
the 2nd-level column: 4 through 24th, 5 from 26th, 6 at 30th (printed p. 171).
the 3rd-level column: 3 at 20th, 4 from 21st, 5 from 26th, 6 at 30th (printed p. 171).
the 4th-level column: 4 through 25th, 5 from 26th, 6 at 30th (printed p. 171).
the 5th-level column: 4 through 25th, 5 from 26th (printed p. 171).
the 6th-level column: 3 at 20th, 4 from 21st, 5 from 28th (printed p. 171).
the 7th-level column: the printed dash at 20th, then 1 at 21st climbing to 5 at 28th (printed p. 171).
the 8th-level column: the printed dashes through 28th, then 1 at 29th and 30th (printed p. 171).

tables.name: dfaFallSurfaceGrid
tables.comment: the fall/jump surface distance grid (printed pp. 172-173): the maximum distance from a vertical surface by level band - 1 foot at 11-13, 2 at 14-16, 3 at 17-19, 5 at 20-21, 7 at 22-24, 9 at 25-27 and 11 feet at 28-30 (row index = the dfaFallBand band).
col_comments: the surface distance column: 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 feet across the seven level bands (printed pp. 172-173).

tables.name: dfaFeatherGrid
tables.comment: the featherfoot surface grid (printed p. 173): three bands (soft - mud, snow, sand; very soft - quicksand, fine dust; liquid - water) with the distance in feet and the movement rate (row index = the dfaFeatherBand band).
col_comments: the surface distance column: 30 feet over soft, 60 over very soft, 120 over liquid (printed p. 173).
the movement column: movement rate 12 over soft, 15 over very soft, 18 over liquid (printed p. 173).

table_checks.note: the Table 50 escape bonds ladder (printed p. 170)
the Table 50 tunneling row with its printed dash (printed p. 170)
